races.name: BetGoodwin Download The App Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Lola De Magny
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making handicap debut off a workable mark but needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: No threat when 3rd on both hurdle runs but this point winner could go well on h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't threatened when third this year on her first two starts over hurdles (2m4f, soft/good to soft) but this 3m point winner now goes handicapping off a realistic mark and could be suited by the step up in trip.

runners_data.name: All Authorized
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who's 10lb lower than last winning mark but disappointing recent form is concerning
runners_data.comment: Disappointing season but now 10lb lower than when winning over C&D last April
runners_data.spotlight: He's had a disappointing season, initially over fences and more recently over hurdles, and has something to prove; however, he's now 10lb lower than when winning over C&D (good) last April and can't be written off; monitor the betting.

runners_data.name: The Wise Traveller
runners_data.note: Only front-runner in field returns from 95-day break, which could either freshen him or leave him short
runners_data.comment: Below par when last seen but break may have helped; C&D win off 3lb higher last September
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who has finished merely seventh on his last three starts, the latest in January; however, a break may have helped and he was returning from some time off when winning under Jamie Gambin over C&D (good) last September; now 3lb lower than for that win and not discounted.

runners_data.name: Hilltown
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with course form but struggled on three recent visits here following long absence
runners_data.comment: Two-time course winner but he's struggled this season (including here) after long absence
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D in April 2023 and a chase here in April 2024; however, he's struggled this season following a long absence, including at this course on three occasions; 4lb out of the handicap; major turnaround needed.

runners_data.name: Local Derby
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with good recent Wincanton win but needs to prove effectiveness on good ground at this trip
runners_data.comment: Progressive 6yo who has won his last two completed starts and holds leading claims
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground 3m point winner who scored at Wincanton (2m4f, heavy) in January on second handicap start, and after an early unseat at Fontwell (jumped path) he returned to winning ways at Exeter (2m7f, good to soft) three weeks ago; this progressive 6yo has leading claims up 6lb for last time.

runners_data.name: Mild Magic
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who hasn't been competitive in five rules runs and needs everything to fall right
runners_data.comment: Step in right direction here last time and the longer trip/better ground may help today
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't been able to get seriously competitive across her five rules runs, in handicaps on last two occasions, but at least her 13l third here (2m4f, soft) in February was a step in the right direction; this 3m point runner-up (good to yielding) could build on it now up in trip and on better ground.

runners_data.name: Barrow Ranger
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making rules debut for Irish connections but point form suggests he needs strong pace
runners_data.comment: Irish raider; hard to fancy on rules form but won a point two starts ago; watch the market
runners_data.spotlight: He's hard to fancy on his rules form and was soundly beaten over fences last time, but he won a point-to-point two starts ago and this 5yo Irish challenger is one to watch in the betting.

races.paceDynamic: The Wise Traveller is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 7-runner field, likely to get an uncontested lead over the extended 3m1f trip. With six hold-up horses behind him including All Authorized, Local Derby, Lola De Magny, Hilltown, Mild Magic and Barrow Ranger, there will be minimal early pace pressure. The Wise Traveller can dictate fractions and kick for home when it suits, while the large pack of hold-up runners will face a tactical nightmare trying to time their runs from the back. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers, as the lack of pace pressure allows leaders to control the tempo and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller gets the easy lead he's seeking and maintains a steady gallop
scenarios.body: The 10-year-old can dictate ideal fractions without harassment and use his superior tactical position to repel late challenges. Hold-up horses face an impossible task trying to make up ground from the back of a slowly-run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong in the middle sections and The Wise Traveller weakens
scenarios.body: The hold-up brigade get the strong pace they need to unleash finishing kicks, with Local Derby and All Authorized best positioned to capitalize. Fresh legs and class tell in the closing stages over this stamina-sapping trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller sets steady fractions but multiple hold-up horses challenge simultaneously
scenarios.body: A messy finish develops with several horses hitting the front in the final furlong, favouring those with tactical speed. The horse who gets the clearest run and times their effort best prevails.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller stops completely and the hold-up horses are caught napping by the crawling pace
scenarios.body: An outsider who positions closer than usual or finds the best ground takes advantage of the tactical confusion. Fresh horses coming from well back pick up the pieces.

watchPoints.text: The Wise Traveller getting loose on the lead - if he's allowed to dictate completely uncontested fractions, the hold-up horses may never get to him
Local Derby's jumping after that early unseat at Fontwell - any mistake will be costly with so much ground to make up from the back
All Authorized's attitude after a series of disappointing runs - needs to show he still has the appetite for a battle
How quickly the hold-up horses commit in the straight - if they hesitate or get in each other's way, The Wise Traveller escapes
The pace through the middle sections - if it stays steady, the front-runner's advantage becomes almost insurmountable

races.name: BetGoodwin Sussex Champion Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Edwardstone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with superior class who should benefit from the strong pace, though 51 days off and advancing years at 12 remain minor concerns.
runners_data.comment: 12yo who showed with Grade 2 win in January he retains considerable spark; leading player
runners_data.spotlight: 12yo whose career highlight came when winning the Tingle Creek in 2022; showed he retains considerable spark when winning Grade 2 at Kempton (2m4f, good) this January; he may prefer a longer trip than this nowadays but he's a leading player nevertheless now back in a handicap.

runners_data.name: Matterhorn
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning after 107 days off who may struggle to control three-way pace battle but has winning form on good ground.
runners_data.comment: Won in good style at Uttoxeter last May; pulled up on sole run since but could bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 5-9 over fences with convincing win at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) last May; pulled up on sole run since, at Ascot in December, but the good to soft ground may not have suited; second in this last year; could go well.

runners_data.name: Kotmask
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose jumping issues this season could be exposed by the strong pace, but ideally positioned tactically if connections have ironed out problems.
runners_data.comment: Jumping issues this term but has good record here; may not be far away if finding fluency
runners_data.spotlight: His jumping has been an issue this season and he was soundly beaten at Newbury last time; however, two starts ago he was a close second of four there (2m, good to soft) and he has a good record at this track; might not be far away if finding some fluency.

runners_data.name: Secret Des Dieux
runners_data.note: Front-runner in excellent current form who faces 7lb rise and must survive expected pace pressure from fellow leaders.
runners_data.comment: 6yo novice; did it very nicely at Kempton last month to make it 3-6 over fences; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Capitalised on the drop back in trip to win at Huntingdon (2m, heavy) in February and followed up at Kempton (2m2f, good); he's 7lb higher than last time and in a hotter race, but did it very nicely and this 6yo novice is now 3-6 over fences; could still have more to offer and he's respected.

runners_data.name: Scorsese
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner carrying bottom weight whose good recent form gives him each-way chances if he can stay in touch with the pace.
runners_data.comment: In good form over 2m3f/2m4f; this trip could suit but he's 4lb wrong at the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Made all at Sedgefield (2m3f, good to soft) on Boxing Day on fourth chase start and his good form has continued when third on both runs since (2m4f, soft/good to soft); this drop back in trip is worth a go and further improvement is possible, but he needs to be better than ever from 4lb wrong.

races.paceDynamic: Matterhorn, Secret Des Dieux, and Scorsese will create a relentless early gallop from the flag, with all three natural front-runners likely to contest the lead through the first circuit. This strong pace will stretch the field and test stamina reserves over Plumpton's demanding 2m1f trip on good ground. The sustained gallop will expose any fitness concerns and create opportunities for horses that can quicken from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses like Edwardstone and Kotmask who can conserve energy and benefit from the inevitable pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too fast early and weaken from 3 out
scenarios.body: The strong early gallop will set up perfectly for hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders in the straight. Edwardstone and Kotmask are ideally positioned to capitalize on their superior class when the pace inevitably crumbles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters can dictate fractions and kick clear
scenarios.body: Secret Des Dieux or Matterhorn could steal a march if they can control the tempo and avoid a punishing duel. Their recent wins show they can quicken when allowed an easier lead than expected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Incident Changes Everything
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or interference disrupts the race flow at a crucial fence
scenarios.body: The strong pace combined with Plumpton's testing fences could cause carnage and completely reshape the contest. Any horse avoiding trouble while others fall or make mistakes gains a decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Genuine Staying Test
scenarios.trigger: If the good ground and honest gallop creates a true test of stamina
scenarios.body: The relentless pace could find out any horse lacking peak fitness or genuine 2m1f stamina. Only the most genuine stayers will be in contention at the business end of this demanding contest.

watchPoints.text: Matterhorn's fitness after 107-day absence could be exposed if forced into early pace battle with Secret Des Dieux and Scorsese
Kotmask's jumping reliability remains questionable after recent errors and the strong pace will test his concentration at Plumpton's demanding fences
Secret Des Dieux faces career-high mark after his recent wins and must prove he can handle the 7lb rise under sustained pace pressure
Edwardstone's market position will reveal connections' confidence in his fitness after 51 days off at age 12
The three front-runners' early positioning will determine whether this becomes a tactical affair or the genuine stamina test the pace suggests

races.name: Roy Reeve Memorial Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Oblemenko
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with unknown ability but comes from a stable with a strong record in this specific race, making him a potential surprise package
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten in both points; check market but others have more compelling credentials
runners_data.spotlight: Brother to bumper/hurdle winner Sansrick (RPR 121); soundly beaten in both Irish maiden points; one of two for stable that has good record in this race; market check advised but others have far more compelling credentials.

runners_data.name: Loriko
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning from a 107-day break who needs the pace to collapse but has proven class when conditions suit
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on handicap debut at Hereford but tough to beat if rediscovering earlier form
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten on handicap debut at Hereford (2m3f) in December when soft going shouldn't have been an issue (ran well on testing ground in France); however, he ran really well in defeat in the autumn on his first three British starts (2m-2m3f, good) and will be tough to beat if rediscovering that form.

runners_data.name: Flash Man
runners_data.note: Promising French recruit who showed improvement last time and represents a trainer with an excellent recent strike rate
runners_data.comment: 2 Flat wins in France; 3rd at Kempton on second hurdle run; can give another good account
runners_data.spotlight: Two-time French Flat winner who was a promising third at Kempton (2m, good) a fortnight ago on his second hurdle start; open to further improvement in this code and can give another good account.

runners_data.name: Tetsworth
runners_data.note: Front runner making hurdle debut for the Moore stable, will need to settle better than his keen flat runs suggest
runners_data.comment: 0-8 on the Flat but with ability; encouraging fourth on sole hurdle start and can improve
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 on the Flat but has shown a fair level of ability in that code, including on last two starts; shaped when fourth of nine on hurdle debut at Kempton (2m, good) in December as though he would improve for that experience; stable has strong record in race; he could be the main threat to Loriko.

runners_data.name: Answer That
runners_data.note: Confirmed early leader but has been tailed off in both hurdle starts, raising serious questions about his jumping ability under pressure
runners_data.comment: Showed promise in bumpers in Ireland but tailed off on first two hurdle starts
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise when making the frame in two bumpers in Ireland (soft to heavy/yielding); however, tailed off on his first two hurdle starts (2m, soft/good to soft) and needs to be an entirely different proposition today.

races.paceDynamic: Tetsworth and Answer That will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front runners likely to ensure an honest gallop from the start. With only five runners, the pace won't be frantic but should be solid enough to test stamina over this 2m trip. The presence of hold-up horses Loriko and Flash Man means the tempo could quicken significantly from the final flight as they attempt to close down the leaders. This race shape favours prominent runners who can track the pace and kick clear, as pure front runners may tie up and pure hold-up horses face too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Tetsworth and Answer That maintain a solid but sustainable pace throughout
scenarios.body: The leaders will have enough left to resist late challenges, with one of the pace-setters or a tracker prevailing. Hold-up horses will find the leaders have too much in reserve when the pace has been controlled.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Decisive
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes pedestrian with the leaders going too slow
scenarios.body: Loriko and Flash Man will have perfect conditions to unleash devastating late runs from off the pace. The hold-up specialists will sweep past tiring leaders who've had no real test of stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Attrition Race
scenarios.trigger: If both front runners go too hard early trying to drop each other
scenarios.body: The genuine stayers will benefit as the pace-setters weaken dramatically from two out. Flash Man's French flat breeding and Loriko's proven stamina will tell in a war of attrition.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moore Stable Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Oblemenko's lightly raced profile masks significant improvement from his point-to-point form
scenarios.body: The stable's good record in this race pays off as their less exposed runner surprises at bigger odds. His brother Sansrick's ability suggests untapped potential waiting to emerge.

watchPoints.text: Answer That's jumping could deteriorate badly if Tetsworth forces a strong early pace, as he's already struggled in previous hurdle starts
Loriko needs the race to unfold at a searching gallop to bring his stamina into play after such a long absence from action
Flash Man showed clear improvement last time and represents Toby Lawes who has a perfect strike rate from recent runners
Tetsworth must prove he can settle kindly over hurdles rather than pulling hard as he did in his flat racing career
The Moore stable's strong record in this race makes both Oblemenko and Tetsworth particularly interesting despite their different profiles

races.name: Southern Cranes & Access Ltd Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Easy Love
runners_data.note: Made all on handicap debut at Windsor but struggled in Grade 2/Listed company on heavy ground, needs to prove this class drop is enough
runners_data.comment: Easily made all at Windsor in January on last handicap start and she's one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: Course bumper winner who easily made all on handicap debut at Windsor (2m4f, good) on New Year's Day; unplaced/pulled up in Grade 2/Listed races on heavy/soft going on her two starts since but she could be an entirely different proposition now back in a handicap and back on better ground.

runners_data.name: Religous Cross
runners_data.note: Showed promise when winning hurdle debut at Taunton but 28-length fourth at Kempton suggests he may need more time
runners_data.comment: Just four runs, with wins in a point/novice hurdle; unexposed and could have more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who scored on his hurdle debut at Taunton (2m3f, good) in December; 28l fourth of 15 in Kempton novice (2m5f, good to soft) since but this unexposed 6yo makes his handicap debut off what looks a fair mark and he could have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Maldini Milano
runners_data.note: Improved when fitted with cheekpieces last time but 78 days off the track is a concern for sharpness
runners_data.comment: C&D maiden winner; weakened on handicap debut but on soft; firmly in calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground bumper winner who got off the mark over hurdles at the third attempt over C&D (good) in November, when wearing first-time cheekpieces (retained) in a maiden that worked out extremely well; weakened into sixth on handicap debut at Windsor in January but that was on soft ground; firmly in calculations now back on a better surface.

runners_data.name: Mount Anglesby
runners_data.note: Progressive for new yard with two wins in last three runs, well-placed to track the early leaders from prominent position
runners_data.comment: Progressive for new yard this term and has won two of his last three starts; respected
runners_data.spotlight: 7yo who has a fair bit of experience but has been progressive for a new yard this term, making it two wins from his last three runs (2m3f/2m5f, good/good to soft) when scoring at Warwick last time; entitled to respect.

runners_data.name: The Boss Bear
runners_data.note: Won last two starts including over course and distance but pulled up and beaten badly in subsequent efforts raises reliability questions
runners_data.comment: Won on hurdle debut over C&D in December but pulled up/well beaten in his two handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Won a bumper at Fontwell (2m1f, good) last May and followed up on hurdle debut over C&D (good to soft) in December; however, he's been pulled up/well beaten in his first two handicaps and needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Minella Jury
runners_data.note: Fell when going well at Wincanton last time after impressive hurdle debut, Sam Twiston-Davies booking is positive
runners_data.comment: Disputing lead when final-flight faller at Doncaster and the winner followed up
runners_data.spotlight: Irish bumper winner (yielding) who followed up on hurdle/stable debut at Uttoxeter (2m, heavy) in December, and he was disputing the lead and clear of the rest when falling at the final flight on handicap debut at Doncaster (2m, good to soft) last time; the winner has followed up off 6lb higher so a 4lb rise for this fellow may well prove lenient; every chance he'll stay.

runners_data.name: Kel Du Large
runners_data.note: Front-running style means he'll ensure a true pace but close second to Mount Anglesby suggests he may lack a finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Listed bumper winner for whom things are clicking over hurdles; possible contender
runners_data.spotlight: Listed bumper winner who scored at Hereford (2m3f, heavy) in February on his third handicap start and was a close second to Mount Anglesby (2m5f, good to soft) four weeks ago; this 6yo could continue to progress now things are starting to click; possible contender in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Tennessee Tango
runners_data.note: Easily won maiden here in February but pulled up in competitive handicap company since, wearing tongue-tie for first time
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in competitive EBF Final at Sandown but progressive previously; not written off
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground bumper runner-up who improved with each of his first four runs over hurdles, easily winning a maiden here (2m, soft) in February; pulled up in the competitive EBF Final at Sandown (2m4f, soft) since and needs to prove his stamina, but pedigree provides hope; not written off.

runners_data.name: High Fibre
runners_data.note: Recent Kempton winner in good form with just seven days between runs, hold-up style suits if pace is strong enough
runners_data.comment: Improved form last month, with a win and a near-miss; could again be thereabouts
runners_data.spotlight: Began to look exposed in the second half of last year but he showed improved form to win at Kempton (2m, good) on March 23 and was short-headed at Ludlow (2m, good) last Monday; he should be fine now back up in trip and could again be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Percy Shelley
runners_data.note: Classy recruit from Flat racing but 135 days absence is a major concern for fitness in this competitive field
runners_data.comment: Useful on Flat; good start to hurdling career; pulled up last time but retains potential
runners_data.spotlight: Useful Flat performer who made good start to hurdling career in the autumn, including when going close in a Cheltenham novice (2m4f, good to soft; has won on good ground); flopped at Ascot (2m5f, good) in November but has had a break since and retains potential now in his first handicap hurdle.

runners_data.name: Jefe Triunfo
runners_data.note: Dropped significantly in weights but 147 days off track and poor autumn form suggests he's not the answer
runners_data.comment: Didn't show enough in handicaps in the autumn to have pressing claims today
runners_data.spotlight: Won a maiden hurdle at Warwick (2m, good) last June and has dropped down the weights, but he didn't show enough in handicaps in the autumn to have pressing claims today; returns from a break.

runners_data.name: Grand Conqueror
runners_data.note: Won two in a row in December but both on softer ground, only five years old with potential upside
runners_data.comment: 2-2 in handicaps before coming clear with well-treated winner last time; lots to like
runners_data.spotlight: Won on handicap debut over C&D (good to soft) in December and followed up at Fontwell (2m1f, good to soft) 11 days later, before clear second to well-handicapped winner at Kempton (2m5f, good to soft) in February; he's up 4lb for last time but the form reads very well and he could settle better in a first-time hood; lots to like.

races.paceDynamic: Easy Love and Kel Du Large will ensure a genuine gallop from the start, with both confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead over this staying trip. The honest pace they set will stretch the field out and create a true test of stamina, particularly with the longer 2m4½f distance allowing no room for error. Mount Anglesby and Tennessee Tango should sit prominent to track the leaders, while the hold-up brigade including Percy Shelley, High Fibre and The Boss Bear will need the pace to collapse late to be effective. This sustained gallop clearly favours prominent racers and those with proven stamina who can sit handy and strike when the pace takes its toll.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop Suits Handy
scenarios.trigger: If Easy Love and Kel Du Large maintain a solid tempo throughout without going too fast early
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will find out the stamina-light horses and set up perfectly for those racing prominently who can quicken when the leaders tire. Mount Anglesby and Tennessee Tango are ideally positioned to benefit from this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Early Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders go too hard early and both tire significantly in the final half-mile
scenarios.body: The excessive early tempo will set up a finish for the hold-up horses who can produce late kicks from off the pace. Percy Shelley and High Fibre have the class and tactical speed to capitalize when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Easy Love Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Easy Love can dictate a more measured tempo and avoid serious early pressure from Kel Du Large
scenarios.body: The Honeyball runner can use his superior class to control the race and kick clear when it matters, making it very difficult for closers to reel him in. His Windsor success suggests he has both the tactical speed and stamina for this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If neither leader wants to make the running early and the pace becomes stop-start
scenarios.body: The lack of consistent tempo will turn this into a tactical affair where horses with natural speed will have the advantage in a sprint finish. This scenario would suit those with turn of foot rather than pure staying power.

watchPoints.text: Easy Love and Kel Du Large could go too fast early if both commit to the lead, potentially setting up the race for closers
Percy Shelley returns after 135 days off but his class could be decisive if the fitness is there in the closing stages
Mount Anglesby has been progressive for his new trainer and is perfectly positioned to benefit from the expected strong pace
High Fibre runs just seven days after his last race which could either keep him sharp or leave him vulnerable late on
Tennessee Tango wears a tongue-tie for the first time which suggests connections are looking for improvement after his last run pull-up

races.name: BetGoodwin Sussex National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Transmission
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 64-day break with Harry Atkins' 7lb claim, won last time by 12 lengths in first-time visor
runners_data.comment: Easily won the Edinburgh National at Musselburgh and an 8lb rise may not stop him
runners_data.spotlight: Tapped back into last season's promising form, and then some, to win by 12l in a first-time visor at Musselburgh (3m7f, good to soft; Edinburgh National) in February; has also won on good ground and 2-2 over hurdles here; an 8lb rise may not stop him if the visor maintains its positive effect.

runners_data.name: Largy Poet
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner back in cheekpieces after pulling up in blinkers, inconsistent but has shown class when right
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent and pulled up last time but back in cheekpieces today and he's not discounted
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent and pulled up in first-time blinkers at Exeter (3m6f, heavy) in February; however, he's back in cheekpieces today in which he kept on for second of six at Wincanton (3m1f, heavy) in January; versatile ground-wise and this sort of trip may yet suit; not discounted.

runners_data.name: Rivers Corner
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter in excellent form with two recent wins, prone to mistakes but thrives when allowed to dominate
runners_data.comment: He's won two of his last three, most recently over 3m6f; clearly on the up
runners_data.spotlight: Easy win at Wincanton (3m2f, heavy) in January and bounced back from Haydock flop to win at Exeter (3m6f, good) recently, despite a bad mistake; clearly on the up and his stable has won two of the last six runnings.

runners_data.name: Invincible Nao
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has won this race before, proven at the trip and grade with strong recent Plumpton form
runners_data.comment: Won this last year and running well in the main this season; chance
runners_data.spotlight: Kicked off 2025 with two wins in a row here (3m1f/3m4f, soft), including this race, and he reappeared with another win at Sandown (2m4f, good) in November; has continued in good form since in the main; chance.

runners_data.name: Sea Invasion
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 51 days off, has won three times on good ground and should be fresh for Anthony Honeyball

runners_data.name: Unanswered Prayers
runners_data.note: 10-year-old hold-up horse who hasn't threatened since winning Southern National, dangerous mark but questionable current form
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark on form as recent as October but this 10yo hasn't threatened since
runners_data.spotlight: Won the Southern National (3m3f, good) in November 2024 and he's on a dangerous mark on form as recent as October 2025; however, this 10yo hasn't threatened since and needs to raise his game.

runners_data.name: Planned Paradise
runners_data.note: Late-running 10-year-old with back-to-back wins on soft ground, faces much hotter contest than recent successes
runners_data.comment: Has won his last two starts in good style; up in the weights but clearly in rude health
runners_data.spotlight: Exploited a reduced mark to win at Bangor (3m5f, soft) in February and again had plenty in hand at Hexham (4m, soft) 12 days ago; this is a hotter race than last time and this 10yo is up 10lb, but he's clearly in rude health and could be bang there once more; handles any ground.

runners_data.name: Tommie Beau
runners_data.note: 11-year-old prominent runner who was second in this race last year, course specialist but struggles off higher marks
runners_data.comment: Strong record here and has a reduced mark but this 11yo is hard to fancy on recent form
runners_data.spotlight: He's won here three times and was second in this race in 2024 on his last Plumpton visit; on a reduced mark but this 11yo has struggled to get competitive on his last few starts and needs to turn things around in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Stans The Man
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from small Ella Pickard yard with 0/2 record in last 14 days, good form at Wincanton last month
runners_data.comment: Back to form to win at Wincanton last month and his revised mark may be within range
runners_data.spotlight: Won two in a row last May (3m5f/3m3f, good) and returned to form to win at Wincanton (3m1f, good to soft) last month following a break; this 9yo has never defied a mark this high but it may be within range if he's once more at the top of his game.

runners_data.name: Havaila
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with course and distance win last March, bounced back to form with recent convincing victory
runners_data.comment: Convincing win at Newbury last month and this progressive 7yo has the necessary stamina
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D (good) last March and reappeared with creditable third of 16 at Windsor (3m4f, soft) in January; bounced back from lesser run with convincing win at Newbury (2m7f, good to soft) last month and this progressive 7yo may be able to take a 9lb rise in his stride.

runners_data.name: Enjoy d'Allen
runners_data.note: 12-year-old prominent runner with three small-field wins this season, faces significant step up in class today
runners_data.comment: Three small-field wins this season; this 12yo may find today's race too competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins in small fields this season (2m5f-3m5f, good/soft) and another good run when second of three at Sedgefield (3m2f, good) recently; however, there's a suspicion this 12yo will find today's race too competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Largy Poet and Rivers Corner are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, creating an honest gallop from the start over this stamina-testing 3m4½f trip. With two natural pacers going at it early, the race will be run at a solid tempo throughout, particularly given Rivers Corner's recent aggressive tactics and Largy Poet's need to use his speed. This sustained pace will set up the race perfectly for the hold-up horses like Transmission, Invincible Nao, and Havaila who can sit off the early battle and produce their finishing kicks. The combination of two keen front-runners and the extended distance strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay and finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Largy Poet and Rivers Corner go too hard early in their front-running duel
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will find out both leaders in the final furlong, allowing the patient hold-up brigade to sweep past with superior finishing kicks. Transmission and Invincible Nao are perfectly positioned to exploit this scenario with their proven staying power.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Rivers Corner or Largy Poet can establish a clear lead and dictate terms
scenarios.body: One of the pace-setters manages to get first run on their rivals and has enough left in the tank to hold off the late challengers. Rivers Corner's recent form and tactical speed give him the edge in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the front two go too slow or too fast, creating gaps
scenarios.body: The horses tracking the pace like Sea Invasion and Tommie Beau can position themselves perfectly to strike when the leaders weaken. Their prominent style allows them to avoid trouble while staying close enough to pounce.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both Largy Poet and Rivers Corner disappoint or fall
scenarios.body: With no natural pace in the race, it becomes a messy sprint where any horse can win regardless of style. This chaotic scenario opens the door for outsiders to capitalize on the lack of shape.

watchPoints.text: Rivers Corner and Largy Poet could go too fast early and set this up perfectly for the hold-up horses behind them
Transmission's 64-day break could be a concern despite Harry Atkins' valuable 7lb claim and his last impressive victory
Invincible Nao has home advantage having won this exact race before and shows consistent Plumpton form
The good going might not suit some of these who have been winning on softer surfaces recently
Sea Invasion's 51-day absence could leave him short of peak fitness despite his excellent record fresh

races.name: Gordon And Angela Ashdown Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: A Tickatickatiming
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong course form who can track Public Enemy without applying early pressure
runners_data.comment: Bumper/maiden hurdle winner here in 2023; in good form and should be close up again
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper and maiden hurdle winner on this course in 2023; has run some good races in defeat here since early last spring and has a chance at the weights with Yasmina on a C&D run in February; improvement not really in the offing but she can be involved.

runners_data.name: Unjeu Royal
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 77-day break with bleeding concerns but useful bumper form for Tom Lacey
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner; promising 2m hurdle form; likely to be competitive on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won Southwell bumper in February 2025; bled from the nose at Lingfield in January but has been ready to run since February and an earlier run, a promising runner-up to a useful one at Huntingdon (2m, good to soft) in November, suggests he will be competitive on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Public Enemy
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who won over course and distance but struggled in handicaps since graduation
runners_data.comment: Won good-ground maiden/novice hurdles last spring but ordinary handicap form so far
runners_data.spotlight: Won good-ground maiden (C&D) and novice hurdles last spring but he ran poorly on handicap debut here in between and his form at this level since hasn't borne much fruit (first-time tongue-tie latest, blinkers now added); however, he may well do better on second run back from a break with Sam Twiston-Davies taking over.

runners_data.name: Risk It All
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with consistent recent form carrying just 157lbs and beaten by a subsequent winner last time
runners_data.comment: French Flat winner but proving hard to place over hurdles so far; needs extra
runners_data.spotlight: French Flat winner in 2024; maiden hurdler who is proving hard to place in handicaps, albeit his latest defeat, over C&D last month, came at the hands of one who'd dropped a long way in the weights; needs more.

runners_data.name: Yasmina
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won over course and distance on handicap debut after wind surgery, now 8lbs higher
runners_data.comment: Had wind op before forging clear of A Tickatickatiming on handicap debut over C&D; up 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Hinted at minor ability before having wind surgery and the operation seemed to help as she forged clear of A Tickatickatiming on handicap debut over C&D (soft) in February; should make a go of it off 3lb higher.

runners_data.name: Fascinating Lips
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse returning after 146-day absence with blinkers applied for the first time
runners_data.comment: Hurdle winner in 2022 but minor form in the autumn and has left the Moores since
runners_data.spotlight: Hurdle winner in 2022 whose latest success came in a classified event (1m2f) last August when with the Moores; minor hurdle form in the autumn and up against it for new yard after a break.

runners_data.name: Galactic Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse claiming 3lb with Freddie Mitchell and gets in on minimum weight of 148lbs

races.paceDynamic: Public Enemy is the only confirmed front runner and will set an uncontested lead from the start, with A Tickatickatiming likely to sit prominent but not pressuring. The 2m trip at Plumpton allows for a sustainable gallop without early burn-up, meaning the pace will be steady rather than fierce. With five hold-up horses (Unjeu Royal, Risk It All, Yasmina, Fascinating Lips, Galactic Jack) needing to come from behind, they'll rely on Public Enemy maintaining momentum throughout. This race shape strongly favours the front runner and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will plague the large pack of hold-up horses in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Public Enemy jumps cleanly and maintains galloping room throughout
scenarios.body: The uncontested lead allows him to dictate terms completely, while the mass of hold-up horses get in each other's way when the pace lifts. Sam Twiston-Davies can time his effort perfectly without pressure from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold Up Revival
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong or Public Enemy makes jumping errors
scenarios.body: The prominent horses set it up perfectly for the closers to sweep past in the final furlong. Risk It All and Yasmina have the best recent form among the hold-up brigade and benefit from lighter weights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If A Tickatickatiming or another prominent runner pressures Public Enemy earlier than expected
scenarios.body: The increased pace compromises the front runner but doesn't set it up completely for the hold-up horses. A Tickatickatiming's course experience becomes crucial in a tactical finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the main fancies underperform or there are significant jumping errors
scenarios.body: Fascinating Lips or Galactic Jack benefit from the chaos while carrying less weight. The veteran Fascinating Lips has course-winning form, while Galactic Jack gets the 3lb claim.

watchPoints.text: Public Enemy's jumping - any early errors will compromise his front-running advantage and change the race dynamic completely
Traffic problems in the straight - with five hold-up horses bunched together, several will get hampered when making their moves
Unjeu Royal's fitness - the 77-day break and previous bleeding episode could see stamina drain away despite his early positioning promise
A Tickatickatiming's tactical positioning - if Marc Goldstein gets closer to Public Enemy than expected it could force an early battle
First-time blinkers on Fascinating Lips - the headgear change suggests connections expect improved focus after the long break

runners_data.name: Hitintheheadlines

runners_data.name: Mint Approved

runners_data.spotlight: One win from four point starts and ran well from the front when back in a bumper and runner-up over C&D (good to soft) last month; others have stronger form but he's open to improvement, especially if settling better.

races.paceDynamic: Cheap Sandwiches and Mint Approved both possess prominent/leading tendencies, but with only four runners this creates a controlled tempo rather than fierce early pace pressure. Cheap Sandwiches likely leads early with Mint Approved tracking, while hold-up specialists Kamille Au Kanada and Hitintheheadlines settle behind the modest gallop. The small field and lack of multiple confirmed pace forces means the tempo will be measured through the early stages, building gradually into a tactical finish. This race shape strongly favours horses with tactical speed and the ability to quicken from prominent positions rather than pure hold-up specialists.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tactical Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Cheap Sandwiches sets a steady tempo without serious early pressure from Mint Approved
scenarios.body: The pace builds gradually allowing prominent runners to maintain position for sustained kicks, negating the usual advantage hold-up horses gain from strong early fractions. Cheap Sandwiches and Mint Approved can use their natural pace to dominate the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes particularly sedate with both prominent runners content to wait
scenarios.body: The crawling tempo transforms into a sprint finish where horses with the best turn of foot prevail regardless of position. Kamille Au Kanada's Irish point wins suggest natural speed while Hitintheheadlines showed promise at Ascot over a shorter trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Cheap Sandwiches or Mint Approved decides to make it a true test of stamina from the outset
scenarios.body: The sustained pace stretches the small field and rewards the horse best suited to the testing conditions over this extended trip. Experience at the distance and proven stamina becomes crucial in a war of attrition.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If both prominent runners hesitate early leaving no clear pace-setter in the opening stages
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical mess with stop-start fractions that suit neither prominent nor hold-up runners consistently. Form and class become the primary factors in a muddled tactical affair.
